name: Khujand International Airport
before:
The airport for Khujand, Tajikistan's second city, in the nearby town of Buston.

The code is a relic. LBD comes from Leninabad, the city's name during the Soviet era, so it does not match the airport's current name at all and can confuse a search.

Traffic has fallen sharply. The airport handled 1,025,537 passengers in 2023 and 779,201 in 2024, a drop of 22.1 per cent, so check what is actually flying rather than relying on an older schedule.

There is a single 3,200 metre runway at an elevation of 442 metres, and a new passenger terminal opened on 1 October 2019.
after:
The airport for Khujand, Tajikistan's second city, near the town of Buston.

Its code, LBD, does not match the city's name, so it can confuse a search.

There is one asphalt runway of about 3,200 metres at an elevation of 442 metres, and a new passenger terminal came into use on 1 October 2019.

claims.note: The Agency on Statistics' 2020 census table (published 2022; columns are 2010 then 2020, each both sexes, men, women) gives the city of Khujand 196,427 in 2020, second to Dushanbe's 948,251; every other city row in the table is smaller (next Bokhtar 124,497, then Kulob 103,541). GeoNames' own population figures are not used here: they rank several whole districts above Khujand.

claims.note: Was 'in the nearby town of Buston'. The coordinates put the airport 2.1 km south of Buston's centre point, which supports 'near'; only Wikipedia says 'in'. The census lists Buston as a town in its own right; GeoNames lists Chkalovsk, the place name in Wikipedia's infobox, among Buston's alternative names.

claims.claim: one asphalt runway of about 3,200 metres
claims.inAfter: There is one asphalt runway of about 3,200 metres
claims.note: Was 'a single 3,200 metre runway'. OurAirports gives 3,180 m and Wikipedia's text 3,200 m, so 'about 3,200'. Wikipedia's infobox (from the Tajik AIP) also lists a 1,650 m grass strip on the same heading, hence 'one asphalt runway' rather than 'a single runway'.

sources.quote: It has one runway designated 08/26 with an asphalt surface measuring 3,200 x 50 m.
The airport resides at an elevation of 442 m above mean sea level.

claims.claim: a new passenger terminal came into use on 1 October 2019
claims.inAfter: a new passenger terminal came into use on 1 October 2019
claims.note: Was 'opened on 1 October 2019'. Asia-Plus quotes the airport's press secretary: the terminal began working on 1 October 2019 as a temporary arrangement for the autumn and winter, 'not yet the official opening'. 'Came into use' is what both sources support; no source for a later official opening was found.

claims.wasBefore: LBD comes from Leninabad, the city's name during the Soviet era
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. GeoNames and OurAirports list Leninabad among the names for the city and the airport, but say nothing of when it was used or of the code. No other saved page mentions it (Tajik Air's history page was read for it). The code itself is kept.

claims.claim: does not match the airport's current name at all
claims.wasBefore: so it does not match the airport's current name at all and can confuse a search
claims.why: Reworded without the Leninabad explanation; the practical point is kept as an opinion.
Rests on the 2023 to 2024 figures, which are cut (below); no 2025 figure was found to show the trend now.

claims.claim: 1,025,537 passengers in 2023 and 779,201 in 2024, down 22.1 per cent
claims.wasBefore: The airport handled 1,025,537 passengers in 2023 and 779,201 in 2024, a drop of 22.1 per cent, so check what is actually flying rather than relying on an older schedule.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and more than a year old. The regional paper it cites (sugdnews.com, February 2025) is behind a Cloudflare block (not retried). No 2025 figure for Khujand was found: Khovar's and Asia-Plus's reports of the Civil Aviation Agency's January 2026 press conference give Dushanbe's total only, and their own day archives for 28 and 29 January 2026 list no Khujand item. The advice to check current schedules goes with the figures.

claims.why: Softened to 'one asphalt runway of about 3,200 metres' (see above).

claims.wasBefore: a new passenger terminal opened on 1 October 2019
claims.why: Softened to 'came into use': the airport called the 1 October 2019 start temporary, not the official opening (see above).

Held back: verified but replaces nothing (the old text names no airline). Somon Air's own About page says it also operates from Khujand and its route finder lists Khujand as one of its two departure points; Asia-Plus (18 Mar 2026) quotes the airline trying to fly Dushanbe to Khujand every day where it can; Wikipedia's infobox gives Somon Air as the hub. For Andy to add if he wants.

sources.quote: The basic airport is the Dushanbe International Airport; the Khujand International Airport is additionally operated.
